I have thoroughly explored the repo. Here is my structured report.

---

# andesim-demo — Repository Study

Repo root: `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo` (git, 24 commits, last work 2026-07-15). It is a **demo-only** repo: every demo is a tiny C program plus a Makefile (and sometimes a `check.sh`). All startup/runtime/linker/BSP infrastructure lives **outside** this repo in the sibling `andesim` checkout.

---

## 1. Top-level structure

### Key files
- `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo/README.md` — the master doc (325 lines; per-demo prose + the engine matrix)
- `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo/ROADMAP.md` — 11 demo entries, one-per-session, with State (`TODO`/`IN PROGRESS`/`DONE`/`BLOCKED`)
- `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo/CLAUDE.md` — only holds the **engine-sweep reporting rule**
- `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo/Makefile` — top orchestrator
- `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo/Make.var` — shared config (paths, toolchain, engine)

### The core idea
> "One ELF runs on every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid` (QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest)."

Each demo links against the andesim runtime (`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the **same binary is engine-portable** — no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

### `SUBDIRS` (the demo list) — `Makefile:5-7`
```makefile
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize
```
15 demo dirs exist on disk (`demo/memsize` is in SUBDIRS; all present). Every demo is registered with a per-mode forwarding rule, e.g. `hello-%: ; $(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@`.

### `make check` — `Makefile:72-86`
Aggregate over `SUBDIRS`: for each demo, if it defines its own `check` target (i.e. has a `check.sh`), run it (real asserts); otherwise assert `make run` exits 0. Continues past failures, prints `ALL DEMOS OK` or `FAILED DEMOS: …` and exits non-zero on any failure. Heavy (coremark/dhrystone run full cycle+hybrid legs). `make check-<name>` runs one demo (`check-%`, `Makefile:137-143`).

### `make check-all-engines` — `Makefile:100-134`
Suite-wide **engine sweep**, capability-gated:
- Parses engines from `andesim list engines` at runtime: `awk '$$2=="vsim" && $$4==64 {print $$1}'` (rv64 vsim engines only). Restrict with `SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b"`.
- For each engine it does a `--dry-run` of a hybrid `hello` and greps the resolved plan; then per-engine it computes `skips`:
  - no `ilm_size=[1-9]` in plan → skip `NEED_LM` (`demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma`)
  - no `hvm_size=[1-9]` → skip `NEED_HVM` (`demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma`)
  - VLEN (`list engines` column 5) empty/`-`/`0` → skip `NEED_V` (`demo/rvv demo/verify`)
- Then runs `make check ENGINE=<eng> SUBDIRS=<non-skipped>` and prints a per-engine `OK (skipped: …)` / `FAILED` summary. A bogus engine → `FAILED`, exit non-zero.

**Gating mechanism (important):** the gate keys off the driver's `--describe`/`--dry-run` output and the `list engines` VLEN column — i.e. what the **vsim wrapper advertises** (LM/HVM *transport* backdoor, VLEN), **not** directly the RTL config. `CLAUDE.md` codifies that every SKIP/FAIL must name the blocking layer (RTL config vs vsim wrapper vs driver vs demo).

### Engines and their features
Three rv64 vsim engines are used. Feature source = `/local/nick/vsim/data/configs/<engine>.cfg` (the live config dir; `andesim/config.env` points `VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`). Confirmed feature values:

| Engine | ILM | DLM | HVM | VLEN | Vector type | Shared cache (CACHE col) |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|------|-------------|--------------------------|
| `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` | 64 KB @0x0 | 32 KB @0x200000 | 256 KB @0x90000000 (2 banks, bank bit 17) | 512 | integer-only (SINT/VDOT/INT4, **no vector FP**) | L2C size 0 → `-` |
| `vsim:ax46mpv_advanced` | 64 KB | 32 KB | 256 KB (bank bit 0) | 512 | integer-only | L2C=0, L3C=0 → `-` |
| `vsim:ax66_makatau` | none (size 0) | none (size 0) | none (no HVM section) | 128 | integer V | L3C **512 KB** → `L3:512K` |

`list engines` column layout (`andesim/driver/cmd_list.cpp:158`):
```
ENGINE  TYPE  KIND  XLEN  VLEN  DLEN  ELEN  CACHE
```
CACHE = platform shared cache (L2C on 45-series, L3C on 46/66); derived by the vsim wrapper from the RTL's `NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`.

### Demo × engine matrix (reproduced from `README.md:238-254`, sweep 2026-07-14/15)

| Demo | ax45mpv_premium | ax46mpv_advanced | ax66_makatau | Blocking layer for SKIP/FAIL |
|------|-----------------|------------------|--------------|------------------------------|
| hello | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| lm | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_slave | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_dma | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| hvm_slave | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| hvm_dma | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| rvv | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| fp | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache/l2c+l3c | SKIP | SKIP | PASS (L3C) | RTL: ax45/ax46 built `NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`; wrapper+driver ready |
| verify | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| syscall | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| coremark | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| dhrystone | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| memsize | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |

Notable history captured in the README: ax46 lm*/hvm* were SKIP until vsim wrapper commit `29f6dbf` added the `set_/get_` backdoor (RTL always had the memories — a **wrapper** gap, not RTL); ax66 syscall FAILED until the HTIF mailbox moved into an **uncached SimControl window** (2026-07-14). rv32 `vsim:d23` and `qemu*` are out of sweep scope.

---

## 2. Per-demo structure and conventions

**Universal layout:** `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; optional `demo/<name>/check.sh` for host-side asserts (see `ROADMAP.md:8-15`). Prebuilt `.elf` and `.dump` artifacts are checked in.

**Universal Makefile shape** (every demo is a copy of this — `demo/hello/Makefile` is canonical):
```makefile
-include ../../Make.var
all: <name>.elf <name>.dump
<name>.elf: main.c ; $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $< -o $@
<name>.dump: <name>.elf ; $(OBJDUMP) -d $< > $@
<name>-fast:          $(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode fast $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<
<name>-cycle:         $(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode cycle  --engine $(ENGINE) ... $<
<name>-hybrid-marker: $(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine $(ENGINE) ... $<
<name>-hybrid-pc:     $(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start <sym> --pc-end <sym>_end ... $<
run: <name>-fast <name>-cycle <name>-hybrid-marker <name>-hybrid-pc
```

**Build:** toolchain from `Make.var`; `CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 -B $(RUNTIME) -specs=andesim.specs`. `-B` puts the runtime's `crt0.o`, `andesim.ld`, `andesim.specs` and `include/` on the search path so `<andesim/ROI.h>` resolves. **Run / the andesim driver command line:** the driver is the wrapper script `$(ANDESIM)/andesim` (`ANDESIM_BIN` in `Make.var`). Four invocations:
- `--mode fast` → QEMU only, full speed, **no cycle figure**
- `--mode cycle --engine <e>` → vsim from reset, cycle-accurate, prints program output + cycle figure
- `--mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine <e>` → QEMU fast-forwards boot; vsim measures between ROI markers; prints `[andesim] N cycles`
- `--mode hybrid --trigger pc --pc-start <sym> --pc-end <sym> --engine <e>` → same window named by ELF symbols, no source markers needed

**ROI markers** (`andesim/build/runtime/include/andesim/ROI.h`): `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()` are RISC-V HINTs (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1`) — architectural NOPs, so one binary runs on all modes and silicon. Contract note: the `"memory"` clobber pins memory but not register-only compute, so the ROI body is a `noinline` non-static function (also gives `--pc-start` a symbol). Convention: a `.globl <name>_roi_end` label right after the call for `--pc-end`.

**How PASS/FAIL is decided** — two mechanisms:
1. **Guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI** (works on hybrid, whose run ends at the exit trigger so nothing after the ROI runs). E.g. `LM_OK`, `RVV_OK`, `FP_OK`, `SYSCALL_OK`, `HVM_SLV_OK`.
2. **`check.sh` asserts on the driver's stdout + exit code.** Pattern (`demo/memsize/check.sh`, mirrored by cache/verify): a portable-bash `assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD…` helper; **no gtest** ("a program's pass/fail is its SimControl exit code + stdout marker; the driver's pass/fail is its process exit code"). Cache/verify additionally parse `[andesim] N cycles` via sed and compare figures.

**Exit code path:** `main()`'s return → `_exit()` writes it to SimControl `0xe0080000` → becomes the andesim process exit code (fast/cycle only; on hybrid the pass signal is the printed marker).

**QEMU staging vs vsim in a run:** In **hybrid**, `main()` before `andesim_ROI_begin()` runs on **QEMU** ("QEMU phase" / staging), which sets up state (fill LM/DLM/HVM, program the DMA controller, seed files, set CSRs). At the begin-marker the driver hands off to **vsim** (cycle-accurate RTL), which executes the ROI and drains the cycle count at the end-marker. The demos exist largely to prove specific state **crosses that handoff** (data via shared mmap or sidecar files `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm`; CSRs like `mcache_ctl`/`fcsr` via the state restore). QEMU can also act as an **oracle**: `--verify` re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU to the ROI exit and diffs drained state field-by-field against vsim.

**Representative demos:**
- **hello** (`demo/hello/`): `main.c` (33 lines) — `say_hello()` prints inside ROI; the minimal template.
- **lm** (`demo/lm/`): enables ILM(`milmb 0x7C0`)/DLM(`mdlmb 0x7C1`), fills DLM with a runtime pattern, assembles a 3-instruction kernel into ILM @0x100, then the vsim ROI re-runs the ILM kernel and checks every DLM word (`LM_OK`). `lm-fast` passes ILM/DLM geometry to plain QEMU via `-- -global driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=ilm_size,value=65536` etc. (`demo/lm/Makefile:18-21`).
- **rvv** (`demo/rvv/`): `<riscv_vector.h>` 8×8×8 int32 GEMM, strip-mined by `__riscv_vsetvl_e32m1` (any VLEN). QEMU stages A/B + scalar ref; ROI computes on the VPU and compares (`RVV_OK`). Integer on purpose — the VPU is integer-only.
- **cache** (`demo/cache/`): two builds from one source (`cache_on.elf`, `cache_off.elf -DCACHE_OFF`), plus `l2c.elf`/`l3c.elf` (one source `l2c.c`, `-DSHC_L3`). `check.sh` parses both hybrid figures and asserts `off > RATIO_MIN*on` (default 2×), and runs the engine-gated L2C/L3C leg (picks L2/L3 from the CACHE column, SKIPs on `-`).

- **syscall** (`demo/syscall/`): one binary exercising stdout(UART), file io + `gettimeofday()`(HTIF window, real host files in cwd), and exit code(SimControl). Demonstrates the two hybrid rules: close FILE*s before the handoff, put must-run code (cleanup) inside the ROI.

<name>.dump: <name>.elf ; $(OBJDUMP) -d $< > $@

**Exit code path:** `main()`'s return → `_exit()` writes it to SimControl `0xe0080000` → becomes the andesim process exit code (fast/cycle only; on hybrid the pass signal is the printed marker).

## 1. Top-level build system

**Key files:** `/local/nick/vsim-demo-new/{README.md, Makefile, Make.var, .gitmodules}`

**Toolchain / config (`Make.var`):**
- `XLEN ?= 64`; `TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX` default points at Andes AST541 newlib toolchain: `.../nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d/bin/riscv64-elf-` → compilers are `riscv64-elf-gcc/g++`.
- `SIMULATOR_BIN ?= /local/nick/vsim/build/sim_ax66` (the vsim binary; overridable, e.g. `sim_ax45mp`).
- `COPILOT ?= .../copilot` — Andes COPILOT (>7.3.0) tool, needed only by ACE demos to compile `.ace` custom-instruction descriptions.
- `OPT_LEVEL ?= -O1`, `INSTALL_PREFIX ?= install`.
- BSP knobs: `PLAT ?= ae350` (or ae250), `MTYPE ?= DDR` (or LM), `INTC ?= plic-novector` (or `plic` vectored, or `aia`), `SMP ?= 1`, `SEMIHOST ?= 0`.
- `BSP_DEFS := -DCFG_MAKEFILE -DCFG_LOAD -DCFG_VSIM -DCLIC_BASE=0` (+ `-DCFG_DDR`, `-DBSP_PLIC -DAPLIC_BASE=0 -DMIF_BASE=0` for the default plic-novector path).

**How a demo is built:** Each `demo/*/Makefile` does `-include ../../Make.var`, sets `CC=$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)gcc`, a per-demo `-march`, and compiles its source together with `$(VSIM_FILES)` and `$(VSIM_FLAGS)` into a bare ELF, plus an objdump `.dump`. Example (`demo/hello/Makefile`):
```make
CFLAGS:= -march=rv$(XLEN)gc $(OPT_LEVEL)
hello: main.c
	$(CC) $^ -o $@ $(VSIM_FILES) $(CFLAGS) $(VSIM_FLAGS)
run: hello
	$(SIMULATOR_BIN) $^
```

**`VSIM_FLAGS` (link options, from `Make.var`):**
```
-nostartfiles -static -Wl,--defsym,_stack=0x3000000 $(BSP_DEFS)
-I bsp_custom -I <bsp> -I <plat> -I <bsp>/driver/include
```
Important: **no `-T` linker script is passed.** Demos link with the toolchain's *default* RISC-V linker script (segments land at `.text`≈`0x10000`, confirmed by the ace-rvv README sim log), NOT the `nds-ddr.ld`/`nds-lm.ld` scripts in `startup-V5`. Only `platform/load_store_demo` adds a section placement (`--section-start=.load_store_pages=0x200000`). The stack is forced to `0x3000000` via defsym; `start-smp.S` gives each hart a `0x100000` slice below it.

**Makefile demo groups (`/local/nick/vsim-demo-new/Makefile`):**
- `CORE_SUBDIRS` (built by `make`, run by `make run`): `cpp, coremark, dhrystone, hello, negative_test, platform, rvv, smp-test, syscall`.
- `EXTRA_SUBDIRS` (built by `make`, need special HW): `hvm_test, lm_test, savable_feat`.
- `ACE_SUBDIRS` (only via `make ace`, need COPILOT): `ace, ace-rvv`. (`acervv46quad` is **not referenced** by the top Makefile.)
- Targets: `make` (=all CORE+EXTRA), `make ace`, `make install` (copies binaries to `$(INSTALL_PREFIX)`), `make run` (runs only CORE_SUBDIRS, aggregates pass/fail via `.test_passed`/`.test_failed` marker files), `make run-<name>`.

**How a demo is run:** `SIMULATOR_BIN=/path/to/sim make run-<name>` → per-demo `run:` target invokes `$(SIMULATOR_BIN) <elf>`. Two demos add `--save` (`hybrid`, `savable_feat`). There is also a BSV path documented in the README.

## 2. Shared infrastructure

### `bsp_custom/` — vsim glue over the BSP
- **`libgloss.c`** (~167 lines): newlib syscall stubs (`_write`, `_read`, `_open`, `_fstat`, `_gettimeofday`, `_sbrk`, …).
  - **stdout/stderr (fd ≤ 2):** `_write` loops `uart_putc()` → real char output. fd > 2 goes through the HTIF frontend syscall to the simulator host.
  - **Program exit / PASS-FAIL signal:** `_exit(status)` writes the status word to `EXIT_COMMAND_ADDR = 0xe0080000` then spins (`1: j 1b`). The simulator watches that address; exit code 0 = success, non-zero = failure. (`EXIT_SUCCESS_CODE 0x01234568` / `EXIT_FAILURE_CODE 0x01234569` are defined but the code actually writes the raw status.)
- **`htif.h`** (~107 lines): Berkeley-HTIF-style host bridge. `frontend_syscall()` fills an 8-word aligned `magicmem[]` buffer and writes a `tohost` command to `TOHOST_CMD_REG = 0xe0080010`; `flush_all_dcache()` (L1 `mcctlcommand` WB+INVAL, plus an L2 CCTL sequence at `0xe0500008/40/80`) runs first so the host sees coherent memory. This is how `syscall`/file I/O reach the host FS.
- **`handler.c`** (~88 lines): installs a `syscall_table` (constructor) and provides strong `syscall_handler()` and `except_handler()` overriding the BSP's weak ones. `except_handler` prints `mcause/mdcause/mepc/mtval` in red and calls `_exit(cause)` — so any unexpected trap ends the sim with a non-zero code.
- **`memory_map.h`** (~38 lines) — the vsim memory map used by the HW-feature demos:
  ```
  RAM         0x0        – 0x7fffffff
  HVM         0x90000000 – 0x9003FFFF
  Hart0 ILM   0xA0000000 – 0xA01FFFFF
  Hart0 DLM   0xA0200000 – 0xA03FFFFF
  SIM_CONTROL 0xe0080000 – 0xe0080fff  (SIM_CONTROL_REG = *0xe0080000)
     TEST_ILM 0x00abcde0  TEST_DLM 0x00abcde1  TEST_HVM 0x00abcde2
  PLDM(debug) 0xe6800000   ACM0 0xc0000000
  ```
- **`syscall.h`** — RISC-V newlib syscall numbers. **`config.h`** is empty (1 line).

### `startup-V5/` (submodule; BSP "libgloss")
- `source/src/bsp/` holds the reset/startup/trap/driver code. Relevant files pulled in by default build: `start-smp.S`, `reset-smp.c`, `initfini.c`, `trap.c`, `lib/printf.c`, `driver/{uart,gpio,pit}.c`, `ae350/{ae350-smp.c, interrupt.c}`.
- **`start-smp.S`** (crt0): sets `gp`, per-hart `sp = _stack - hartid*0x100000`, enables FPU/vector in `mstatus` when `__riscv_flen`/`__riscv_vector`, sets `mtvec=trap_entry`; hart 0 calls `__platform_init` then `reset_handler`; secondary harts park in `wfi` until MSWI then also call `reset_handler`. `trap_entry` saves GPR/FPR context and dispatches to `interrupt_entry` / `except_entry`.
- **`reset-smp.c` / `reset.c`:** `reset_handler` runs init arrays and `_exit(main())` (SMP) / `exit(main())` (non-SMP). So **a demo signals success simply by `return 0` from `main`**; failure by `exit(nonzero)` or an uncaught trap.
- **`ae350/platform.h`** aggregates `core_v5.h, ae350.h, interrupt.h, uart.h, gpio.h, pit.h, plic.h, clic.h, aplic.h, imsic.h` and defines device pointers (`DEV_PLMT`, `DEV_UART2`, …). `ae350.h` has the full AE350 MMIO map: `PLIC 0xE4000000`, `PLMT 0xE6000000`, `PLIC_SW 0xE6400000`, `SMU 0xF0100000`, `UART1 0xF0200000`, `UART2 0xF0300000`, `PIT 0xF0400000`, `GPIO 0xF0700000`, etc. `core_v5.h`/`csr.h` provide `read_csr/write_csr/set_csr/clear_csr` and NDS CSR numbers (`NDS_MHARTID 0xf14`, `NDS_MICM_CFG 0xfc0`, `NDS_MHVM_CFG 0xfd0`, `NDS_MHVMB 0xfd1`, `NDS_MILMB 0x7c0`, …).
- `startup-V5/source/src/demo/` and `template/` contain a *separate*, larger AndeSight demo/BSP set (aia, cache, clic, iopmp, mmu, pma, pmp, smp, wfi, …) that the vsim-demo Makefiles do **not** build — potential extra source if you want more demos, but not wired in here.

**vsim-specific mechanisms to know when porting:** exit port `0xe0080000`; HTIF `tohost` at `0xe0080010` + `magicmem`; sim-control trigger reg `0xe0080000+0x20` (interrupt injection); sim-control command reg writes `0x00abcde0/1/2` to make a simulator "custom master" DMA into ILM/DLM/HVM; L2 CCTL at `0xe0500000`. These are all backdoors the RTL/csim model must implement.

# Port demos from vsim-demo-new into andesim-demo

## Context

The old suite `/local/nick/vsim-demo-new` has 17 demos. The task: study which ones are worth moving into `/home/nick/work/andesim-demo` (the andesim driver demo repo: one ELF, three modes - fast/QEMU, cycle/vsim, hybrid).

Study result (verified against sources, engine cfgs, runtime, and vsim platform code):

| vsim-demo-new demo | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| hello, coremark, dhrystone, rvv, syscall | already covered | direct equivalents in SUBDIRS |
| lm_test, hvm_test | already covered | lm/lm_slave/lm_dma + hvm_slave/hvm_dma use real transports, not the sim-control backdoor (0xe0080000 = 0xabcdeX) |
| hybrid, savable_feat | covered by design | the repo's hybrid mode + `verify` demo ARE the save/restore story; driver has no --save/--resume |
| **atomic-test** | **PORT NOW** | rv64gc baseline; no infra gap; nothing in andesim-demo tests LR/SC/AMO |
| **negative_test** | **PORT NOW** | andesim runtime handler.c already prints `[ERROR] ... mcause` and `_exit(mcause)`; only a check.sh is missing |
| cpp | TODO (runtime gap) | `andesim/runtime/crt0.S` calls `init_mtvec` directly and never walks `.init_array`; C++ static ctors will not run; `andesim.specs` has no C++ libs |
| smp-test | BLOCKED | all registered engines have `NDS_NHART=1`; mp2 cfgs exist (`ax45mpv_mp2`, `ax66_mp2`, NHART=2) but no engine is built/registered; runtime `CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=0`; driver has no multi-hart handoff |
| platform pit/plic/aia | BLOCKED | `vsim_andesim/src/platform/` models only UART/SMU/SimControl - no PLIC/PLMT/PIT; QEMU ae350 has them, so cycle/hybrid legs are impossible until the vsim platform grows them |
| ace, ace-rvv | NOT PORTABLE | need COPILOT toolflow + csim lib (`libaceasim.a`) baked into the simulator build; QEMU cannot execute ACE custom instructions, so fast mode, hybrid staging, and the --verify oracle all break |
| acervv46quad | NOT PORTABLE | sources missing (only a Makefile referencing absent files + a private GEN_API tool) |

Deliverable: two new demos (`demo/atomic`, `demo/trap`), ROADMAP entries for the study outcome, README sections + matrix rows, engine sweep of the new demos reported per CLAUDE.md rule.

## Feature 1: demo/atomic (from atomic-test)

New files: `demo/atomic/main.c`, `demo/atomic/Makefile`.
Edits: top `Makefile` (SUBDIRS + `atomic-%:` forwarding rule), `README.md` (section + matrix row), `ROADMAP.md` (entry, state DONE when merged).

Design - port the 4 tests, with one deliberate change:
- T1: LR/SC pair succeeds (sc=0) and commits the value. (as source)
- T2 REDESIGNED: source T2 breaks the reservation with a same-hart store; the ISA only guarantees SC failure for other-hart writes, so QEMU (value-compare cmpxchg) and RTL (monitor) could legitimately diverge. Replace with the architecturally-guaranteed case: LR, SC (succeeds and consumes the reservation), second SC to the same address MUST fail and MUST NOT write ("executing an SC invalidates any reservation held by this hart"). State this in a comment.
- T3: amoswap.w returns old value, writes new. (as source)
- T4: 5x amoadd.w +7 on 100 == 135. (as source)

# Ports from /local/nick/vsim-demo-new (study 2026-07-15)

Entries 12-16 come from a port study of the old vsim demo suite. Same rules:
one session builds ONE entry. The study's "no port needed / not portable"
verdicts are recorded at the bottom so the analysis is not redone.

## 12. atomic

State: TODO
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `atomic-test`.

LR/SC + AMO contract on every engine - nothing in the suite touches the A
extension today. Four tests in a `noinline` `atomic_kernel()` inside the
ROI: (T1) LR/SC pair succeeds and commits; (T2) after an SC consumes the
reservation, a second SC to the same address must fail and must not write;
(T3) `amoswap.w` returns old, writes new; (T4) 5x `amoadd.w` +7 on 100
== 135. T2 is a deliberate redesign: the source demo broke the reservation
with a same-hart store, which the ISA leaves implementation-defined (QEMU's
value-compare cmpxchg and the RTL monitor may legitimately diverge);
SC-after-SC failure is architecturally guaranteed on both. Every LR/SC pair
stays entirely inside the ROI - a reservation is microarchitectural and
cannot cross the QEMU->vsim handoff. The target variable is a
`static volatile uint32_t` in .bss (plain DRAM). No engine gating: A is
baseline on all three engines.

- Key files: `demo/atomic/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `ATOMIC_OK` from inside the ROI only if all four
  tests pass; exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none.

State: TODO

printed marker, and this demo's whole point is the exit-code contract).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `negative_test`.

A faulting guest must fail loudly on every engine. main prints a banner,
then executes an illegal instruction (`.insn r 0x7f, 0, 0, x0, x0, x0`,
fallback `unimp` if engines disagree on mcause). The runtime already does
the rest: `handler.c` prints `[ERROR] Trap occurred! ... mcause: 0x2` and
`_exit(mcause)`, so the driver exits 2. The `run:` target inverts (`!`) so
a correct fault reads as success; `check.sh` (memsize assert helper)
asserts rc==2 AND `Trap occurred` on stderr for both the fast and cycle
legs - loud failure if the guest does NOT trap or the cause differs.

- Key files: `demo/trap/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh green on both legs, on every engine.
- Deps: none.

Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid once unblocked.
Origin: vsim-demo-new `cpp`.

C++ on the andesim runtime. Blocked because `runtime/crt0.S` calls
`init_mtvec` directly and never walks `.init_array`, so C++ static
constructors never run; `andesim.specs` also links no C++ library. Unblock

demo is a small `main.cpp` whose pass string is assembled by a
static-constructor-initialized object plus `std::string`/`std::vector` use.

- Key files: `demo/cpp/{main.cpp,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;

State: BLOCKED (no multi-hart engine registered)

Every registered engine is single-hart (`NDS_NHART=1`). Multi-hart RTL
configs exist (`ax45mpv_mp2`, `ax66_mp2`, NHART=2) but no engine is built
or registered from them. The runtime parks secondary harts

register an mp2 engine, rebuild the runtime with `CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=1`,
then teach the handoff N harts. The vsim platform already models the SMU
(`smu.hpp`), so the source demo's core-count read (SYSTEMCFG 0xf0100008)
